claim: The multi-line value syntax shown for --env-file (MULTI_LINE="THIS IS\nA MULTILINE") does not work on Node v20.6.0 through v20.11.x, because the history tables state multi-line support was added in v21.7.0 and v20.12.0 and the v20.6.0 page documents only one-line key=value pairs.
would_change: Changes 'Node's --env-file supports multi-line values' to 'supports them only on >= v20.12.0 / >= v21.7.0'; a .env file with quoted multi-line values must be flattened for anything pinned to v20.6.0-v20.11.x.

claim: The rule 'An error is thrown if the file does not exist' holds for --env-file but not for --env-file-if-exists, which was added only in v22.9.0.
would_change: Changes 'loading an optional env file always risks a startup crash' to 'only on Node < v22.9.0'; on >= v22.9.0 the optional-file case is handled by switching flags rather than by guarding the file's existence externally.

claim: N11 is titled 'fs.watch() Caveats: recursive restriction removed' but the excerpt contains no mention of the recursive option or of any restriction being removed; it lists only platform backends and Windows caveats.
would_change: Removes any support for the claim that recursive fs.watch became unrestricted in v20.19.0; a decision to rely on recursive watching would have to be re-sourced from the actual v20.19.0 fs docs before being acted on.

claim: The two excerpts describing which quote characters --env-file strips disagree on the character set: N01 lists '\, " or ' while N04 lists '`, " or ', and neither excerpt's own example uses the disputed first character.
would_change: Blocks the conclusion that backticks (or backslashes) are valid value delimiters in a .env file; until the live cli.html page is checked, only double and single quotes can be relied on.

claim: N02 states both that 'the value from the environment takes precedence' over a file value and that with multiple --env-file arguments 'subsequent files override pre-existing variables defined in previous files', without saying whether 'pre-existing variables' includes variables that came from the real process environment.
would_change: Determines whether `node --env-file=.env --env-file=.development.env` can override an exported shell variable; if it cannot, layered env files cannot be used to force per-environment overrides on machines where the variable is already exported.

claim: N09 states the Permission Model restricts File System access behind --allow-fs-read while N02 states --env-file reads a file from disk at startup, and neither excerpt says whether --env-file loading is subject to that restriction.
would_change: Determines whether running with --permission requires an explicit --allow-fs-read entry for the .env path; if it does, every permission-model deployment using --env-file needs an extra flag or it fails at startup.
